General_DataPanel_Description: Access and manage your projects and designs.
General_Browser_Description: View and control the visibility of objects that make up your design.
General_Timeline_Description: View and edit your design history.
General_WorkspaceMenu_Description: Switch to a different workspace to access different capabilities.
General_End_Title: Revisit the tour anytime from the Help menu.
GeneralPartAssembly_DataPanel_Descriptio: Access and manage your projects and designs.
GeneralPartAssembly_Browser_Description: View objects that make up your design, set units, and switch between Part, Assembly, and Hybrid design types.
GeneralPartAssembly_Timeline_Description: View and edit your design history.
GeneralPartAssembly_WorkspaceMenu_Descri: Switch to a different workspace to access different capabilities.
GeneralPartAssembly_End_Title: Revisit the tour anytime from the Help menu.
Gerative_OpenSample_Start_Description: We'll guide you through setting up a generative study.
Gerative_OpenSample_GeometryTypes_Descri: Choose areas to keep or remove in the generative outcomes.
Gerative_OpenSample_DesignConditions_Des: Add constraints and loads to simulate real-world conditions.
Gerative_OpenSample_DesignCriteria_Descr: Set objectives and manufacturing constraints for the generative outcomes.
Gerative_OpenSample_Outcomes_Description: Generate design alternatives that meet your study requirements.
DrawingsFlow1StartDescription: Take a quick tour of the Fusion interface, find helpful recommendations, and switch to the Drawing workspace.
DrawingsFlow1Step1Description: Look in the File menu to see the options for creating designs.
DrawingsFlow1Step2Description: Use the Data Panel to upload, access, and manage your data. Uploaded designs are saved in the All Projects subsection.
DrawingsFlow1Step3Description: Look at our samples in the Data Panel for hands-on experience and inspiration.
DrawingsFlow1Step4Description: See useful information that helps you as you work. You’ll get feature recommendations, tips and more.
DrawingsFlow1Step5Description: Generate 2D drawings from your designs to help with your manufacturing process.
DrawingsFlow1EndDescription: Go ahead and start creating your next great idea.
DrawingsFlow2StartDescription: Learn how to place a base and projected view, add dimensions and add text and notes.
DrawingsFlow2Step1Title: Create a base view of your design
DrawingsFlow2Step1Description: Place a base view on the sheet. Later, you can use it to generate additional views.
DrawingsFlow2Step2Description: Create projected orthogonal and isometric views of the design.
DrawingsFlow2Step3Description: Select objects and place a dimension.
DrawingsFlow2Step4Description: Use these commands to add text and notes to sheets in a drawing as you document your design.
DrawingsFlow2EndDescription: Go ahead and start creating your next great idea.
DrawingsFlow3StartDescription: Learn how to create a drawing template, create placeholder views and add your drawing info to the title block.
DrawingsFlow3Step1Description: Look in the File menu to create a new drawing template so you can set up consistent standards for new drawings.
DrawingsFlow3Step2Title: Start your files the way you want
DrawingsFlow3Step2Description: Select your preferences and then click OK to start your Drawing Template from scratch.
DrawingsFlow3Step3Description: Click Base View to set the first view in your drawing template.
DrawingsFlow3Step4Description: Include the geometry and information about the design in your title block so you can reuse it in the future.
DrawingsFlow3Step5Description: Go here to view or change standard, units, text, dimension, line type, width and color settings for your drawing. You can also access the Automation tab.
DrawingsFlow3EndDescription: Go ahead and start creating your next great idea.
SurfacingFlow1StartDescription: Learn where to find the Surfacing tab in Fusion, create a sketch, and then check out common and advanced modeling tools.
SurfacingFlow1Step1Title: Use surface tools to create stylized designs or repair imported geometry
SurfacingFlow1Step1Description: Use surface modeling when the shape of a design can’t be created easily with solid modeling features.
SurfacingFlow1Step2Title: Create a sketch as a base for your design
SurfacingFlow1Step2Description: You can use an open or closed sketch profile to create a surface body.
SurfacingFlow1Step3Title: Use these common tools to create surface bodies
SurfacingFlow1Step3Description: You'll find tools like Sweep, Extrude, Revolve, and Patch in the Create panel.
SurfacingFlow1Step4Title: Try more advanced shape and repair tools
SurfacingFlow1Step4Description: You'll find additional surfacing tools, such as Loft, Patch, Ruled, and Offset in the Create menu.
SurfacingFlow1EndDescription: Explore the surfacing tools and create your design from scratch
SurfacingFlow2StartDescription: Learn where to find the Surfacing tab and explore the modify, stitch, unstitch and trim tools in Fusion.
SurfacingFlow2Step1Title: Clean up incomplete data on imported geometry
SurfacingFlow2Step1Description: Use surface modeling tools to patch holes or replace bad surface data on imported geometry to make water tight solids.
SurfacingFlow2Step2Description: Use tools like Extend, Trim and Stitch to change the surfaces in your design.
SurfacingFlow2Step3Title: Stitch surfaces to make a single body
SurfacingFlow2Step3Description: Use the Stitch tool to join multiple surface bodies into a single body, or even into a manifold solid body.
SurfacingFlow2Step4Title: Separate faces into a multiple bodies
SurfacingFlow2Step4Description: Unstitch solid bodies or multi-faced surface bodies into discrete surface bodies.
SurfacingFlow2Step5Title: Remove unwanted sections from a surface or quilt
SurfacingFlow2Step5Description: Split intersecting surfaces and remove one or more sections.
SurfacingFlow2EndDescription: Explore the surfacing tools and add to your design.
SurfacingFlow3StartDescription: Learn where to find the Surfacing tab, discover common tools, and see how this design was built in Fusion.
SurfacingFlow3Step1Title: Use surface tools to create stylized shapes and designs
SurfacingFlow3Step1Description: Use surface modeling when the design shape is difficult to accomplish with solid modeling features.
SurfacingFlow3Step2Description: Create or make changes to your surfaces in your design.
SurfacingFlow3Step3Title: Watch how this model was made
SurfacingFlow3Step3Description: Click play to walk through the features in the timeline which show exactly how this model was created.
SurfacingFlow3Step4Description: In the timeline, right-click Loft2 and select Edit Feature to open the feature dialog and explore feature-specific settings.
SurfacingFlow3EndDescription: Discover more about how this model was created.
GenerativeFlow1StartDescription: Take a quick tour of the Fusion interface, learn how to open the uploaded design, and switch to the Generative Design workspace.
GenerativeFlow1Step1Description: Use the Data Panel to upload, access, and manage your data. Uploaded designs are saved in the All Projects subsection.
GenerativeFlow1Step2Description: In the Data Panel, double-click your design to start making changes.
GenerativeFlow1Step3Description: Start working with your design to create multiple alternatives that meet your requirements.
GenerativeFlow1Step4Description: Use the study to set up a design problem by specifying geometric, performance, and manufacturing requirements.
GenerativeFlow1Step5Description: Move along the toolbar from left to right, using each command to set up your study.
GenerativeFlow1EndDescription: Set up your first study and discover a new way of designing. Learn more
GenerativeFlow2StartDescription: Take a quick tour of the Generative Design workspace to learn the key steps in setting up and generating a study.
GenerativeFlow2Step1Description: Use Preserve Geometry, Obstacle Geometry, and Starting Shape to define where the material can be added or removed from the final shape of your design.
GenerativeFlow2Step2Description: Apply constraints and loads that reflect the real-world conditions.
GenerativeFlow2Step3Description: Specify objectives and manufacturing constraints to define the design goals for the solver.
GenerativeFlow2Step4Description: Use the commands from the Generate panel to check study settings, preview, and generate outcomes.
GenerativeFlow2EndDescription: Once you’ve specified the design requirements, you can generate the outcomes. Learn more
GenerativeOutcomes_StartDescription: We’ll guide you through exploring outcomes for a generative study.
GenerativeOutcomes_OutcomesDescription: Explore multiple outcomes to find the best one.
GenerativeOutcomes_FilterDescription: Display the outcomes that interest you most.
GenerativeOutcomes_ViewsDescription: Explore generative outcomes in the way that works best for you.
GenerativeOutcomes_SelectOutcomeDescript: Double-click a generative outcome to explore it in more detail.
GenerativeOutcomes_CreateDesignDescripti: Create a design or mesh design from a generative outcome.
GenerativeOutcomes_EndTitle: Revisit the tour anytime from My Fusion page
Dora_StaticStress_NewGuidedResults_Descr: Read a summary of your Safety Factor result, and see Next Steps suggestions, in the Guided Results panel.
Dora_StaticStress_Results_Description: Inspect all the results, to understand your model’s performance better.
Dora_StaticStress_Inspect_Description: Use toolbar tools to explore your results, uncover patterns, compare data, and answer specific questions.
Dora_StaticStress_Plots_Description: Track how the result changes with each iteration of the solution process.
Dora_StaticStress_Animate_Description: For results with result steps, animate them with the animation bar that appears at the bottom of the canvas.
Dora_StaticStress_Visualizations_Descrip: Select different result visualizations from the Result Settings, to focus on specific areas of interest.
Dora_StaticStress_Classic_Description: To return to the classic experience, deselect “New Simulation Results UI” in user Preferences.
